title: Twenty one soldiers held a fort against thousands - and won a place in history by losing.
sources: Civilsdaily - Why September 12 is observed as Saragarhi Day
India Sentinels (India Defence News) - What is the Battle of Saragarhi that India commemorates on September 12
caption:
Twenty one soldiers held a fort against thousands - and won a place in history by losing.

On the Samana Ridge of the North-West Frontier, a garrison of 21 Sikh soldiers from the 36th Sikhs, led by Havildar Ishar Singh, faced a tribal force numbering in the thousands - vastly outnumbered, with no realistic hope of reinforcement in time.

All 21 soldiers died holding the post - buying critical time for two nearby forts to prepare their defenses. The British Parliament held a rare standing tribute in their honor and all 21 were posthumously awarded the Indian Order of Merit, the era's highest gallantry honor open to Indian soldiers.

September 12th is observed as Saragarhi Day - a Regimental Battle Honours Day for the Sikh Regiment and a state holiday in Punjab since 2017. Nearly 130 years later, the standard it set for holding a position against impossible odds is still the one referenced.
